title: MEG loses momentum as textile chain demand stays subdued
summary:
Global MEG prices retreated in the week to September 18, 2026, ending a four-week climb as sluggish polyester and textile demand weighed.
MEG CFR India fell 5.5 per cent to $0.744 per kg; Southeast Asia dropped 5.8 per cent to $0.784 per kg on the week.
Domestic China slipped 0.9 per cent to $1.046 per kg but stayed 18.1 per cent above late August, while FD NW Europe eased to 0.859.

title: Gucci made its $1,000 sneaker in China and luxury is paying attention
summary:
Gucci’s $1,000 The Drip is made in China, signalling luxury sourcing is shifting towards technical footwear capability.
China’s ecosystem covers bonding, moulding, engineered textiles and rapid prototyping; TexPro says Europe-bound footwear exports hit $8.76 billion in Jan-Aug 2026.
Italy keeps its edge in leather goods and heritage footwear, while technical sneakers may move to specialised.

title: Performance Days CEO to debut on fossil-free performance panel
summary:
Performance Days will expand its Munich education programme on October 13–14, 2026, covering bio-based materials, PFAS alternatives, circularity and EU rules.
For the first time, chief executive officer Marco Weichert will join an expert panel to discuss the road towards fossil-free performance.
New education formats will connect textile sourcing with practical innovation and compliance guidance.

title: India’s weavers seek six-month duty relief as yarn costs rise
summary:
Indian weaving representatives have urged the finance ministry to remove basic customs duty on MEG, PTA, POY, FDY and DTY for 6 months to ease polyester input costs.
The call follows price rises: PTA to ₹106.50 (~$1.11) per kg, polyester melt to ₹120.05 per kg and polyester staple fibre up ₹2 per kg from September 26.
Industry comments warned pressure could affect employment but did not quantify job losses.

title: China PFY falls and Pakistan rises: Why are Asia markets diverging?
summary:
China’s PFY ex-mill grades declined across the tracked range in the week ended September 25, with FDY 100D/72F down 3.03 per cent.
India’s DTY 150D/48F held at ₹157.50/kg (~$1.64/kg), while Pakistan’s POY and DTY rose 1.75 per cent and 1.20 per cent.
TexPro data point to divergent pricing conditions across China, India and Pakistan, shaped by demand, duties and input costs.

title: Pakistan cotton reprices 5.61% as Asian markets pull apart
summary:
Asian cotton markets moved in different directions in the week ended September 25, 2026, according to TexPro daily benchmarks.
Pakistan's KCA spot fell 5.61 per cent, from PKR 525.24/kg on Monday to PKR 495.77/kg on Tuesday.
China's BCI 3128B 28 mm rose 0.20 per cent over the week, while India's Shankar-6 stayed unchanged at ₹195 per kg.

title: Fashion shopping moves from websites to AI: Who controls the sale?
summary:
Coach and Kate Spade can now be bought inside Gemini and Google Search AI Mode in the US, while Nike and Shopify join Google’s agentic shopping push.
For apparel, product data on fit, fabric behaviour, care, occasion and use can shape AI recommendations before shoppers reach brand websites.
Brands may gain faster conversion but lose upsells, loyalty enrolment and behavioural data.

title: India’s PSF prices rise as domestic PTA, melt costs increase
summary:
Indian PSF prices increased by ₹2 (~$0.02) per kg from September 26, after a ₹3 per kg rise on September 16.
Domestic PTA rose to ₹106.50 per kg and polyester melt to ₹120.05, while MEG stayed at ₹83.70.
The revisions lifted 1.4 denier PSF to ₹146 per kg, with cumulative gains of ₹5 per kg; CFR China PTA ended $40 per tonne above September 18.
No new filament yarn revision was indicated.

title: China’s industrial profits rose 15.7% in first eight months of 2026
summary:
China’s industrial profits rose 15.7 per cent year on year to 5.27 trillion yuan in the first eight months of 2026, driven by strong gains in manufacturing and high-tech industries. 
Manufacturing profits rose 17.4 per cent year on year to nearly 3.97 trillion yuan, while August industrial profits increased 4.2 per cent, extending the double-digit growth trend.

title: US, China advance trade ties with $30 bn tariff-treatment framework
summary:
The US and China have operationalised bilateral trade and investment boards to address tariff treatment, market-access barriers and investment-related issues. 
They agreed on recommendations covering $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction and are continuing discussions on critical-mineral supply chains, including rare earths, developments relevant to global importers and sourcing teams.

title: India apparel’s next growth test: Can scale translate into profit?
summary:
India’s domestic apparel market is shifting from revenue growth towards profitability, retention, productivity and capital discipline.
DaMENSCH raised ₹17.40 crore (~$1.81 million) from A91 Partners and Tancom Electronics at a broadly flat valuation of about ₹600 crore in early September 2026.
ABFRL reshaped Pantaloons, re-entering Nagaland as its national store count edged down.

title: $28 bn in apparel, $2.6 mn detained: Can US customs track the cotton?
summary:
TexPro records $27.30 billion of HS61–62 apparel exports from Vietnam to the US in November 2024–June 2026, close to a $28 billion estimate.
Vietnam imported $2.355 billion of US raw cotton, but China supplied $2.589 billion of cotton yarn and woven cotton fabric.
UFLPA can follow upstream inputs across borders; proving fibre origin inside a finished garment remains harder.

title: BGMEA opens Japan Desk to boost Bangladesh's apparel exports
summary:
BGMEA has launched a Japan Desk in Dhaka to link Bangladeshi garment factories with Japanese buyers and support market diversification.
Around 100 factories have been selected for buyer-supplier matchmaking, market information and issue resolution.
The association targets apparel exports to Japan of $3 billion by 2030, up from about $1.4 billion.

title: India’s shirt exports lead H1 garment trade despite 13.8% fall
summary:
India’s garment exports fell 11.2 per cent to $7.882 billion in January–June 2026 from $8.880 billion a year earlier.
Shirts stayed the largest category at $1.430 billion, followed by T-shirts at $1.148 billion and dresses at $1.138 billion.
Cotton garments accounted for $4.686 billion, while woven garments formed 55.76 per cent of exports.

title: Bangladesh's RMG exports to UK rise 3.74% in July-August
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports to the UK rose 3.74 per cent year on year to $915.63 million in July-August FY2026-27, supported by a 10.53 per cent increase in August that offset a 2.44 per cent decline in July. 
The two-month earnings were 20.86 per cent of full-year FY2025-26 UK RMG export earnings of $4.39 billion, indicating a stronger start to the new fiscal year.

title: Austria’s apparel imports shift towards Asia before EU parcel duty
summary:
Austria’s apparel imports rose nearly 2 per cent to $3.785 billion in January–June 2026, with Asia-Pacific shipments up 104 per cent to $788.673 million.
Europe remained the top source at $2.817 billion, but its share fell to 74.43 per cent from 86.56 per cent as imports declined by about 12 per cent.
Trousers and shorts led categories at $1.009 billion, or 26.68 per cent of total imports.

title: Fashion’s climate push: Clean power becomes a supplier capability
summary:
Levi Strauss & Co. and Marks & Spencer launched the Fashion Renewable Collaborative in New York to help mills and factories access renewable electricity.
Cascale’s Athens meeting put financing, accountability and business value at the centre of supply-chain transformation.
The platform combines supplier-energy programmes and supports power purchase agreements, certificates, on-site generation.

title: Japan’s apparel imports grow 6.6% to $2.3 bn in July 2026
summary:
Japan's apparel and accessories imports rose 6.6 per cent year on year to 371,963 million yen (~$2.36 billion) in August 2026.
Textile yarn and fabric imports climbed 16.9 per cent, while exports grew 10.4 per cent during the month.
Textile machinery exports rose 24.0 per cent to 27,984 million yen in August and 11.7 per cent to 160,129 million yen in January-June 2026.

title: EU Philippines FTA opens €514 mn apparel sourcing opportunity

TexPro shows H1 2026 EU27 imports from the Philippines up 45.8 per cent in HS6110 sweaters, 16.7 per cent in HS6203 and 10.0 per cent in HS6204.
Rules of origin, capacity and compliance will decide if preferential access becomes durable EU business.

title: Luxury demand polarises: How is the fashion supply chain responding?
summary:
First-half 2026 results show luxury demand concentrating at the top end as higher prices and softer discretionary spending curb aspirational buyers.
Prada Group revenue rose 16 per cent at constant exchange rates to €3.048 billion (~$3.46 billion), while Hermès grew 6.1 per cent.
Moncler EMEA, Ferragamo wholesale and Gucci show pressure, prompting reassessment of pricing, product mix and distribution.
